card: Bitcoin Core aborts FlushStateToDisk early with an error if flushing block or undo data files fails. Previously, a block-file flush failure requested shutdown but still proceeded to write block-index metadata and coins data, advancing the recorded flush marker despite incomplete persistence. This could cause on-disk chainstate and downstream persistent indexes to record blocks that were never made durable. The change resolves a TODO from PR #27866 and adds a unit test verifying that flush markers and coins DB state do not advance on failure.
changed_since_previous: The implementation and test were split across two commits to separate the characterizing test from the validation fix, with minor test adjustments.
evidence: Resolves a long-standing TODO in validation.cpp deferred from PR #27866: '// TODO: Handle return error, or add detailed comment why it is safe to not return an error upon failure.'
Author notes PR #34897 introduced m_last_flushed_block to prevent persistent indexes from committing ahead of chainstate, an invariant broken if the marker advances despite failed flushes
problem: When FlushChainstateBlockFile() fails, shutdown is requested, but FlushStateToDisk() continued executing anyway. It wrote block-index metadata and coins cache updates to disk and advanced m_last_flushed_block, potentially recording blocks as durable whose underlying block or undo data was never safely flushed.

risk.why: A bug in chainstate flush error handling could lead to unhandled flush failures or unexpected state when flushing during shutdown.

summary: Aborts FlushStateToDisk() immediately if flushing block or undo data files to disk fails. This prevents writing block-index metadata or the coins database and stops m_last_flushed_block from advancing when block data could not be made durable.
